ordered_diagnoses: Multiple Hereditary Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinomas

s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple skin-colored papules on the face and vulva with a gradual increase in number over time
salient_findings: Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules on the face and vulva
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age and gradually increased
Family history of similar facial papules
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules are present on the face and vulva
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age
Lesions gradually increased to approximately 60
Patient has a medical history of meningioma
Family history is notable for a daughter with similar facial papules
No palmar or plantar pits were observed
Histopathology showed buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces
Clefting between tumor aggregates and the surrounding stroma was focally evident
Whole-exome sequencing revealed a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene

shortlist: Multiple Hereditary Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinomas

shortlist.label: Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's presentation of multiple skin-colored papules, family history, and genetic findings (SUFU gene mutation) are consistent with this diagnosis.

shortlist.label: Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology showing buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces supports this diagnosis.

shortlist.label: Gorlin Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome, Gorlin Syndrome is also characterized by multiple basal cell carcinomas, and the patient's medical history of meningioma is a known association.

shortlist.label: Multiple Hereditary Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinomas
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's family history and the presence of multiple infundibulocystic basal cell carcinomas make this a plausible diagnosis.

shortlist.label: Basal Cell Nevus Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Although similar to Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome, the presence of basal cell nevi and the patient's age of onset are consistent with this diagnosis.

shortlist.label: Bazex Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's presentation of multiple skin-colored papules on the face and vulva, although less common, could be consistent with Bazex Syndrome.

shortlist.label: Brooke-Spiegler Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's family history of similar facial papules and the presence of trichoepitheliomas (although not explicitly mentioned) make this a possible diagnosis.

shortlist.label: Rombo Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's presentation of multiple skin-colored papules, although not typical, and the absence of other characteristic features (e.g., palmar or plantar pits) make this a less likely but still plausible diagnosis.
